breaking.headline: Consumer confidence surges to 103.3, highest since January 2025
breaking.fact: The Conference Board's confidence index jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, up from 91.9 in October and far above the roughly 92.4 forecast — its highest since January 2025. The present-situation gauge rose to 132.8 and expectations to 83.6, with the survey crediting brighter job prospects and easing post-midterm uncertainty.

breaking.headline: U.S. prepares to raise tariffs on China and other countries
breaking.fact: Higher levies targeting excess industrial capacity overseas are expected this week, Dow Jones reports, in a fresh escalation of the trade fight just days after last week's Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen. The move would land on top of the fragile tariff truce that runs into January.

breaking.headline: Nvidia sinks 8% as Monday's record rally reverses
breaking.fact: Nvidia fell about 8% to near $152 in late-morning trading, deepening its premarket slide and giving back part of Monday's record 31% surge. Chip stocks are leading the retreat, with the Nasdaq down more than 2% and Micron, AMD and Marvell also sharply lower as the AI rally cools.

breaking.headline: Democrats plan new taxes on investment income and estates
breaking.fact: Democrats plan to attack income inequality with higher top income-tax rates, a surtax on millionaires and lower estate-tax exemptions, Dow Jones reports, putting investment taxes squarely on the post-midterm agenda. The proposals are a wish list for now, but they frame the tax debate heading into next year.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide ticked up in Paris to €188.10, worth $206.21 at the ECB's Nov 24 reference rate of 1.0963. The industrial-gas giant is drifting higher while U.S. tech gives back Monday's historic gains, its defensive profile on full display. The euro sparkline shows a slow, orderly drift with no break in either direction. With no company news in play, the dollar price from here mostly tracks the euro's moves.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic slid 11.5% to $77.55 on Tuesday, falling below its $83 IPO price a week after listing as the AI trade unwound. The listing is barely a week old, so the tape is still finding its level after the debut pop, and the drop came with chips and memory names leading the retreat. Watch whether $83 flips from support to resistance now that the stock trades beneath it.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up 0.02% to $91.62, its usual slow grind as the Treasury bill ETF accrues interest. The fund keeps paying its monthly distribution — $0.30849 per share, ex Nov 2, paid Nov 5 — and the distribution yield sits at 4.04%. It is the quiet corner of the watchlist: no drama, just steady Treasury income. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, short rates stay the story here.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet fell 1.5% to $277.96 on Tuesday as the AI trade cooled after Monday's 6.3% surge. The pullback is broad — chips and memory names are leading the retreat — rather than anything specific to Google. The stock still sits well above its recent lows after Monday's record-setting session. The next catalyst is Wednesday's inflation data ahead of the Fed's December meeting.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Lilly rose 3.0% to $1,406.06 on Tuesday, climbing with drugmakers after Sanofi's $41 billion deal to buy Insmed put a spotlight on the sector. The move extends Monday's 1.3% gain and keeps the stock near the top of the watchlist's gainers. Big-pharma M&A is back in fashion, and Lilly's pipeline makes it a name buyers keep circling. Watch whether the sector strength holds once the deal headlines fade.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere edged up 0.4% to $296.72 on Tuesday as oil prices rebounded from Monday's slide, with Brent back above $90. The LNG exporter is holding near its highs while energy markets weigh abundant supply against the shipping risks in the Middle East. U.S. gas exports stay the long-run story, and the Strait of Hormuz remains the swing factor. A calm strait would take some of the premium back out of energy.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia sank 8.0% to $151.80 on Tuesday, giving back part of Monday's record 31% surge after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Chip stocks led the retreat across the market, with Micron, AMD and Marvell also sharply lower. The SEC probe, the California review and Huang's Dec 1 House testimony are still open. Sean's call stands: long-term hold until the probes shake out.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer climbed 3.2% to $28.28 on Tuesday, rising with drug stocks after Sanofi's $41 billion deal to buy Insmed rekindled pharma M&A. The move is one of the day's better showings on a tape that is otherwise giving back Monday's gains. Pfizer's dividend yield keeps it a steady income name while the sector consolidates. Watch whether deal fever spreads to other large drugmakers this week.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab tumbled 9.3% to $45.01 on Tuesday as growth and space names led the market's give-back after Monday's historic rally. The drop erases most of Monday's 9.3% gain, leaving the stock roughly where it started the week. No company news is driving the move — it is the risk-off tape, not the rocket business. The next company catalyst is the launch manifest, which stays busy into year-end.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 2.3% to $8.35 on Tuesday, one of the few green names as stocks gave back Monday's rally. The mortgage REIT keeps grinding higher on its dividend appeal while the 10-year yield eases toward 4.89%. Its servicing and origination mix benefits when rates stop climbing. With a December Fed hike near-certain, the rate path and the mortgage market stay the things to watch here.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: The SPAC index fund fell 6.5% to $124.74 on Tuesday as speculative names led the market's retreat from Monday's surge. The drop gives back most of Monday's 4.4% gain in a single session, a reminder of how fast this basket moves both ways. Small, speculative issues are the first to be sold when the tape turns risk-off. The fund needs a steadier tape before its holdings can rebuild momentum.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist was essentially flat at $46.86 on Tuesday, drifting 0.1% lower while the broader market gave back Monday's gains. The regional bank is holding its ground as the 10-year yield eases and investors reassess the December Fed hike. Banks are caught between higher-for-longer rates and a softer economy. The next read comes Wednesday, when inflation data lands ahead of the Fed meeting.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony dropped 8.7% to $2.18 on Tuesday as speculative miners sold off with the risk-off tape. The slide comes even as China extended its suspension of antimony export curbs to Jan 27, easing the supply-squeeze thesis for now. The stock had bounced 7.2% on Monday off its lows, and the bottom watch re-armed this week. Watch whether the $2 level holds as the next test of the recent base.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy fell 5.4% to $5.53 on Tuesday, giving back part of Monday's 10.2% jump as risk names sold off. The uranium story itself is unchanged — UEC remains a favorite on its strong balance sheet and the nuclear build-out theme. The bottom watch that re-armed Monday stays live, and the stock is still well above Friday's $5.30 low. A steadier tape should let the uranium thesis reassert itself.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero slipped 0.3% to $328.35 on Tuesday even as crude prices rebounded, with WTI back above $81. Refiners are caught between rising crude costs and the softer demand picture, and the stock is taking a breather after Monday's 1.4% decline. The position stays locked in the portfolio, so the move is noise either way. Watch the crack spread and the Strait of Hormuz for the next direction.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund holds a $28.51 NAV, unchanged from Monday since mutual funds price daily after the close. The balanced fund's equity sleeve did the heavy lifting in Monday's rally while its bond holdings steadied the ride. It is the set-and-forget core of the watchlist, rebalancing itself as 2035 approaches. The December Fed meeting is the next event that could move its bond side.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P 500-anchored estimate puts VI5TC at $146.83, down 1.3% with Tuesday's market pullback after Monday's rally. The estimator tracks the S&P 500's move from its Nov 3 anchor, and Sean's own check put it within about 0.1% of the real price. The fund's actual holdings are index-linked, so the estimate moves tick-for-tick with the market. A steadier tape should lift the estimate back toward $149.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund holds its $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 3.78%, published Nov 23 by Schwab. The sweep vehicle keeps shrinking as Sean moves balances over $1,000 into CDs, per the November plan to wind it down. The inherited-IRA slice is exempt from the nudge until March. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, money-fund yields may edge up rather than down.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds its $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.03%, published Nov 23 by Vanguard. It remains the top-yielding cash on the watchlist and the parking spot for the ANT proceeds and the Seiver Slough and Lodge sale streams in the income model. The fund owns only Treasuries, so it carries no credit risk. A December Fed hike would likely lift its yield further.

weekInBrief.headline: China keeps antimony and chip-material curbs on hold until January
weekInBrief.body: China's Commerce Ministry extended its suspension of export bans on gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the U.S. through Jan 27, 2027, days after the Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen. The pause had been due to expire Friday, and graphite export reviews stay eased. For U.S. Antimony watchers, the supply-squeeze thesis is on hold for two more months.

weekInBrief.headline: AI shocks are rattling the next generation of mathematicians
weekInBrief.body: Two surveys reported by Nature show early-career mathematicians anxious about AI's advance: 70% of graduate-student respondents said they are now more likely to consider careers outside academia, and only about 7% think AI will make landing a professorship easier. The backdrop is Anthropic's claimed Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, still being scrutinized by the field.

weekInBrief.headline: 156-million-year-old 'dragon' fossil identified in Wyoming
weekInBrief.body: Researchers have identified a previously unknown reptile from a 156-million-year-old fossil found in Wyoming's Meilyn Quarry in 2022, naming it Meilynodraco amonamarthi after a Swedish metal band. The 18-inch creature, with two dragon-like horns on its head, was identified with neutron imaging and X-rays; the study appears in Royal Society Open Science.

weekInBrief.headline: Nearly 7,000 digital brain twins built to study dementia
weekInBrief.body: An international team built personalized computer models of 6,986 human brains from functional MRI data to study how aging, environment and neurodegenerative disease shape brain function. The digital twins, published Nov 23 in Nature Biomedical Engineering, offer a new way to test how individual brains respond to disease and treatment.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Monday called the U.S. naval blockade “military aggression” and said Tehran will use all available tools to confront it, while Foreign Minister Araghchi called talks on reopening the strait “pointless” until Iran's demands are met. Iran's navy said Tuesday that two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire, a day after the Revolutionary Guard claimed three tankers struck mines under U.S. escort — neither claim has been independently verified and no vessels have been named. Marine Traffic data show crossings fell from 226 in the first week of November to 125 in the week to Nov 23, down more than 40%, and Treasury Secretary Bessent unveiled fresh Iran sanctions on Tuesday. Iranian crude exports remain near zero since the blockade was restored on July 14 — TankerTrackers says one tanker loaded Iranian crude by ship-to-ship transfer last week, though Tehran dismissed the report as speculation — while Gulf oil keeps flowing through the strait, with about 4.2 million barrels aboard ships that crossed in the past 24 hours, per AIS tracking, virtually all of it non-Iranian.

space.headline: Webb's dust maps show a star's layers mixed hours before it exploded
space.body: The James Webb Space Telescope mapped the dust of supernova remnant Cassiopeia A clump by clump, finding silica-dominated dust in one region, carbon dust in another, and magnesium silicates in the “Green Monster.” The pattern points to a shell merger — the star's oxygen- and carbon-burning layers mixing — just hours before it exploded. The study was published Nov 23 in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

space.headline: Pakistani astronaut to become first foreign visitor to China's space station
space.body: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani military pilot, will fly aboard China's Shenzhou-24, launching Wednesday at 8:18 a.m. Beijing time with commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. As payload specialist he will run biotechnology experiments during about a week aboard Tiangong, then return on Shenzhou-23 — the first foreign astronaut to visit the station.

space.headline: Brain claims a hand as its own before it is even touched
space.body: Karolinska Institutet researchers tracked brain activity millisecond by millisecond as 45 volunteers experienced the rubber-hand illusion, finding three waves of ownership activity that begin about 80 milliseconds before a brush touches the skin. The right hemisphere leads, then the left joins in — evidence that expectation shapes the sense of body ownership. Published Nov 23 in Nature Communications.

space.headline: Deepest volcanic eruptions ever found, 6,148 metres down in the Mariana Trench
space.body: A robot submarine sampling the Mariana Trench's inner wall near Challenger Deep found pyroclastic rocks from explosive volcanic eruptions at 6,148 metres — the deepest such deposits ever documented. The find, published Nov 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science, is startling because immense water pressure should suppress explosive eruptions, and the forearc should be too cool to melt.

apod.title: Spiral's Edge
apod.credit: NASA, ESA, Michael Jones (California Institute of Technology); Image Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America)
apod.explanation: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image released Oct. 16, 2026, features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way-like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth.
